question: Which Mughal Emperor has attempted to vandalise the Kailash Temple at Ellora?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mughal emperor who is often attributed with attempts to vandalise the Kailash Temple at Ellora is:**
 
• **Aurangzeb**
 
 
• Aurangzeb, whose full name was **Abul Muzaffar Muhi-ud-Din Muhammad Aurangzeb, ruled the Mughal Empire from 1658 to 1707.**
 
• He is known for his strict adherence to **Islam and the implementation of Islamic laws during his reign.**
 
• Aurangzeb was known for his military campaigns and extended the Mughal empire to its **greatest extent**.
 
• However, his** religious policies are often blamed for causing resentment among his Hindu subjects, which included the destruction or desecration of Hindu temples.**
 
• Reports suggest that he attempted to vandalise the** Kailash Temple at Ellora, an example of his iconoclastic policies, although the temple survived largely intact.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **Kailasha Temple Ellora**

 
 
• ​__The Kailasha Temple is the largest of the rock-cut Hindu temples at the Ellora Caves, Maharashtra.
 
• It is considered one of the most remarkable cave temples in the world because of its size, architecture and sculptural treatment, and the climax of the rock-cut phase of Indian architecture.
 
• The Kailasa temple is the largest of the 34 Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu cave temples and monasteries known collectively as the Ellora Caves, ranging for over 2 kilometers along the sloping basalt cliff at the site.
 
• The temple architecture shows traces of Pallava and Chalukya styles.
 
• The temple contains a number of relief and free-standing sculptures on a grand scale equal to the architecture, though only traces remain of the paintings which originally decorated it.

 Shah Jahan is best known for commissioning the Taj Mahal, a mausoleum for his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal. He also constructed the Red Fort and the Jama Masjid, among other architectural feats.
 
 

 Babur
 1526-1530
 Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India, is known for his memoir, the Baburnama, which provides detailed insights into his life and times. He also established the basis for Mughal architecture in India.
